packing: Summit layers: pack puffy/fleece, long pants and a windproof shell for Haleakalā even when Kīhei is 88°F.
Ocean kit: rash guards, mineral sunscreen, water shoes, dry bags and medically appropriate motion-sickness supplies.
Road kit: offline maps, phone mount, water and food for Hāna/Haleakalā; never rely on summit services.
Rain/trail kit: grippy shoes and light shells for Kauai; a sunny coast does not predict Kōkeʻe or Hāʻena.

Field Notes

How to keep two famous islands family-sized

The plan is disciplined about what it does not stack.

Maui

Two high-output drives, separated

  • Haleakalā and Hāna never run back-to-back without a beach reset.
  • Pīpīwai is excluded from the Kīhei round trip.

South Kauai

Weather buffer before moving

  • Nā Pali is booked early enough to shift once.
  • Waimea uses lookouts plus one family trail, not a canyon endurance hike.

North Kauai

Reservations outrank wish lists

  • Hāʻena is a permit-dependent day with a full alternate.
  • Hanalei is swimmable only under live lifeguard/runoff guidance.
